_comment: PREPARED, NOT ACTIVATED. Drafted wording guidance for the account owner's eventual mailbox, kept in the repository so it can be reviewed before anyone uses it. It activates NOTHING on its own. Using it requires, in order: (1) institutional IT approval of the Gmail OAuth application - the last attempt returned Error 400 admin_policy_enforced; (2) a SEPARATE institutional decision approving transmission of recruit email content, which may involve minors, to Gemini - Gmail approval does not cover this, and Gemini currently runs on a personal API key, which is a production governance issue to resolve first; (3) taxonomy discovery run against that account, since these categories are drafted rather than discovered; (4) the account owner personally running approve_account.py and typing the confirmation; (5) an AI-drafting approval artifact bound to that account. Every drafting mode below stays inert until those exist. Note every category is 'generic' EXCEPT 'other', which is off and routes to Needs Review. No protected label is configured here: a year label needs a protected_labels entry plus an evidence_gated_labels rule, and AI drafting on protected-label messages needs allow_protected_labels plus the longer confirmation phrase including messages under protected labels. The display_name, organization, signature, and guidance below are PLACEHOLDERS. Replace them with the account owner's real details before use; a draft generated as-is would sign with the wrong name.

taxonomy.description: A prospective student-athlete introducing themselves and expressing interest.
taxonomy.label: Recruiting/Triage/Recruit Introduction

drafting.guidance: Thank the student for introducing themselves and for their interest in the program. Briefly acknowledge specific information they provided. Encourage them to stay in touch and to send meaningful updates. Do not claim film was watched or that they are being actively recruited unless the message itself establishes it.

taxonomy.description: A recruit sharing a schedule, academic, athletic, or recruiting update.
taxonomy.label: Recruiting/Triage/Recruit Update

drafting.guidance: Thank the student for the update and mention the specific event, schedule, result, or development they shared when appropriate. Do not promise attendance, evaluation, or follow-up by any particular date.

taxonomy.description: A recruit sharing highlight film or a new video link.
taxonomy.label: Recruiting/Triage/Video Update

drafting.guidance: Thank the student for sending the video and acknowledge what they sent without claiming it has already been watched. Say the staff will review it when appropriate. Never provide a fabricated evaluation.

taxonomy.description: A parent or guardian writing about a prospective student-athlete.
examples: Writing on behalf of my son
taxonomy.label: Recruiting/Triage/Parent or Guardian

drafting.guidance: Thank the parent for reaching out and keep the reply courteous and factual. Do not disclose private recruiting information, make commitments concerning the student, or invent admissions or recruiting policy.

taxonomy.description: A question about a clinic, camp, registration, timing, or logistics.
taxonomy.label: Recruiting/Triage/Camp Inquiry

drafting.guidance: Answer only from approved camp facts supplied in account context. Never invent dates, locations, pricing, availability, or registration links. If the required information is unavailable, acknowledge the question and say the coach will follow up.

taxonomy.description: A club, high-school, or college coach contacting the program.
taxonomy.label: Recruiting/Triage/Other Coach

drafting.guidance: Thank the coach for contacting the program and stay professional. Do not disclose confidential evaluations, recruiting status, or information about another student.

taxonomy.description: Legitimate human administrative, operational, or institutional correspondence.
taxonomy.label: Recruiting/Triage/Administrative

drafting.guidance: Draft only a neutral acknowledgement. Do not confirm payments, contracts, reservations, account changes, deadlines, or institutional actions.

taxonomy.description: A legitimate human message that does not fit another reviewed category.
taxonomy.label: Recruiting/Triage/Other Human Email

ai_drafting.signature:
The Account Owner
Head Coach
Example College
ai_drafting.default_guidance: Write as the account owner, head coach at the configured organization. Produce a concise, warm, professional reply that responds only to information present in the current message and the approved account context. Never promise or imply admission, recruitment, a roster position, playing time, financial aid, a scholarship, an offer, or any future evaluation outcome. Never invent dates, registration links, prices, schedules, policies, or facts. Do not infer a graduation year; the application's independent evidence gate decides that. Do not repeat sensitive personal information unnecessarily. Do not mention internal classifications, labels, automation, or AI. If the reply would require facts you do not have, write a brief acknowledgement and say the account owner will follow up rather than guessing. Before returning, silently verify the draft contains no invented fact, promise, evaluation, or registration detail; does not claim any attachment or video was reviewed; does not infer recruiting status or graduation year; and is an acknowledgement rather than an acceptance, commitment, or decision. Return only the email body.
